title: Randomised open-label pilot Study on Thiamine supplementation to REduce braiN injury associated with chronic Alcohol use in outpatients with alcohol use disorder : STRENA
official: Randomised open-label pilot Study on Thiamine supplementation to REduce braiN injury associated with chronic Alcohol use in outpatients with alcohol use disorder : STRENA
summary: Main objective: The primary objective is to evaluate the efficacy of a 14-day course of thiamine supplementation in reducing brain damage, as measured by plasma levels of light neurofilaments (NFL), in patients who are chronic alcohol users and have an alcohol use disorder, using an intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients being treated for moderate or severe alcohol use disorder
2. Reported daily alcohol consumption of at least 40 g
3. Patients aged 18 to 65
4. A urine pregnancy test performed prior to enrollment for women of childbearing age
5. Use of contraception for women of childbearing age who are sexually active
6. Enrollment in a social security program or the Aide Médicale d’État program, or eligibility for such a program.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Use of thiamine within the past month
2. Pregnant and breastfeeding women
3. Known or suspected allergy to any of the ingredients in the investigational drug Bevitine (thiamine)
4. Known or suspected wheat allergy (other than celiac disease)
5. Fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption syndrome, or sucrase-isomaltase deficiency
6. Planned hospitalization during the study period
7. Scheduled surgical procedure under general anesthesia during the study period
8. History of Wernicke’s encephalopathy, delirium tremens, or severe cognitive impairment
9. Epileptic seizure, stroke, or severe head trauma within the last three months
10. Active infection with HIV, hepatitis C virus (HCV), or syphilis
11. Glomerular filtration rate (GFR) <50%
12. Severe renal impairment (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²)
13. Individuals subject to legal guardianship, conservatorship, or trusteeship
sponsor: Institut National De La Sante Et De La Recherche Medicale
